---
title: "Install MISP 3.0 on OpenBSD 8.0"
---

This guide installs the latest [MISP `3.0_wip` branch](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/tree/3.0_wip) on a clean OpenBSD 8.0 amd64 host.
It uses the packaged Apache, PHP 8.3, MariaDB, Redis, and Supervisor services. [OpenBSD 8.0 release](https://www.openbsd.org/80.html)
The setup was exercised in a native OpenBSD 8.0 amd64 virtual machine.

::: {.callout-note}
`3.0_wip` is the MISP 3.0 development branch.
Evaluate it on an isolated host before deployment.
Use these steps for a new database. For an existing MISP 2.5 instance, see [Plan a 2.5 upgrade](#openbsd-install-upgrade).
:::

## Prepare the host {#openbsd-install-prepare}

Use the default OpenBSD install sets, including `comp80.tgz` for Python extension builds and `xbase80.tgz` for the PHP GD dependencies.
Make sure the filesystem containing `/var` has space for both the application checkout and MariaDB data, plus temporary space for imports.
Use a DNS name and a TLS certificate chain and private key for that name.
Restrict initial HTTPS access to administrators until the bootstrap password is changed. [Instance requirements](../requirements/index.qmd)

Apply the current OpenBSD patches with `syspatch` and reboot if required.
Run the host commands in a root shell and use `/etc/installurl` to select your package mirror. [OpenBSD package management](https://www.openbsd.org/faq/faq15.html)

```bash
pkg_add apache-httpd bash composer curl git gnupg mariadb-server redis supervisor \
  'php-apache%8.3' 'php-curl%8.3' 'php-gd%8.3' 'php-intl%8.3' \
  'php-pcntl%8.3' 'php-pdo_mysql%8.3' 'php-zip%8.3' pecl83-apcu pecl83-redis \
  py3-pip py3-jsonschema py3-lxml py3-magic py3-zmq ssdeep unzip--
```

Select Redis 8 if `pkg_add` prompts for a branch.
The port provides PHP as `/usr/local/bin/php-8.3`.
On a clean host, create the `php` link used by MISP's Cake wrapper and enable the extensions from their packaged configuration samples.

```bash
ln -s /usr/local/bin/php-8.3 /usr/local/bin/php
for extension in apcu curl gd intl pcntl pdo_mysql redis zip; do
  ln -s "/etc/php-8.3.sample/$extension.ini" "/etc/php-8.3/$extension.ini"
done
php --version
php --ri pdo_mysql
php --ri redis
```

In `/etc/php-8.3.ini`, set `memory_limit = 2048M` for the initial definitions import and PHP runtime.

## Install MISP and its dependencies {#openbsd-install-source}

Use OpenBSD's `www` account for the Git checkout, dependency installation, and Cake commands.
Run those commands from a directory `www` can access, such as `/var/www`, because `su -m` preserves the working directory.
Clone the latest branch with the submodules it selects.

```bash
install -d -o www -g www -m 0750 /var/www/MISP /var/db/misp \
  /var/db/misp/composer /var/db/misp/attachments
cd /var/www
su -m www -c 'env HOME=/var/db/misp git clone --branch 3.0_wip --depth 1 \
  --recurse-submodules --shallow-submodules \
  https://github.com/MISP/MISP.git /var/www/MISP'
su -m www -c 'env HOME=/var/db/misp git -C /var/www/MISP status --short --branch'
su -m www -c 'env HOME=/var/db/misp COMPOSER_HOME=/var/db/misp/composer \
  composer --working-dir=/var/www/MISP/app install --no-dev --no-interaction --prefer-dist'
su -m www -c 'env HOME=/var/db/misp COMPOSER_HOME=/var/db/misp/composer \
  composer --working-dir=/var/www/MISP/app check-platform-reqs --no-dev'
```

### Install the Python helpers {#openbsd-install-python}

Create a virtual environment that can use OpenBSD's packaged `pip`, XML, JSON Schema, magic, and ZeroMQ libraries.
The OpenBSD package set and Python package index used for this guide had no ready-made OpenBSD build of LIEF.
Use a copy of the checkout's Python requirements with the LIEF line removed.
Binary metadata extraction that depends on LIEF is unavailable with this setup. [MISP file-object diagnostic](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/blob/3.0_wip/app/files/scripts/generate_file_objects.py)

```bash
su -m www -c 'env HOME=/var/db/misp python3.14 -m venv \
  --without-pip --system-site-packages /var/www/MISP/venv'
awk '$0 !~ /^lief([<>=!~]|$)/' /var/www/MISP/requirements.txt \
  > /var/db/misp/python-requirements.txt
chmod 0644 /var/db/misp/python-requirements.txt
su -m www -c 'env HOME=/var/db/misp CPPFLAGS=-I/usr/local/include \
  LDFLAGS=-L/usr/local/lib /var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python -m pip install \
  -r /var/db/misp/python-requirements.txt'
su -m www -c '/var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python -m pip check'
```

## Initialize MariaDB, Redis, and MISP {#openbsd-install-database}

In `/etc/my.cnf`, set `bind-address = 127.0.0.1` in the `[mysqld]` section and leave the local socket available.
In `/etc/redis/redis.conf`, keep Redis bound to loopback with protected mode enabled.
If the Redis sample enables `loadmodule ./modules/…` for Bloom, Search, JSON, or TimeSeries, comment out those lines. The OpenBSD package tested here lacks those modules, and Redis exits if it tries to load them.
Create the MariaDB system tables once on the new host and enable both daemons. [OpenBSD service control](https://man.openbsd.org/rcctl.8)

```bash
mariadb-install-db
rcctl enable mysqld redis
rcctl start mysqld redis
redis-cli ping
env MYSQL_HISTFILE=/dev/null mariadb --protocol=SOCKET
```

When Redis is ready, it returns `PONG`.
In the MariaDB session, create a dedicated database and account for the loopback TCP connection.
Substitute a unique password and retain it for the database configuration.

```sql
CREATE DATABASE misp CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci;
CREATE USER 'misp'@'127.0.0.1' IDENTIFIED BY 'REPLACE_WITH_DATABASE_PASSWORD';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON misp.* TO 'misp'@'127.0.0.1';
EXIT;
```

Load the schema from that checkout and copy its application configuration templates.

```bash
mariadb --protocol=SOCKET misp < /var/www/MISP/INSTALL/MARIADB.sql
for name in bootstrap config core database; do
  install -o www -g www -m 0640 \
    "/var/www/MISP/app/Config/$name.default.php" "/var/www/MISP/app/Config/$name.php"
done
```

In `/var/www/MISP/app/Config/database.php`, set `host` to `127.0.0.1`, `login` to `misp`, and `password` to the database password.
Keep `database` set to `misp`.
Set these keys in the `MISP` section of `/var/www/MISP/app/Config/config.php`, using your hostname and organization.

```php
'baseurl' => 'https://misp.example.org',
'external_baseurl' => 'https://misp.example.org',
'org' => 'Your organization',
'osuser' => 'www',
'python_bin' => '/var/www/MISP/venv/bin/python',
'attachments_dir' => '/var/db/misp/attachments',
'redis_host' => '127.0.0.1',
'background_jobs' => false,
```

Set `Security.salt` to a unique value from `openssl rand -hex 32` in the same file.
Keep jobs disabled while you apply schema updates, create the first administrator, and import the bundled definitions.

```bash
su -m www -c '/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin runUpdates'
(umask 077; su -m www -c '/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake User init' \
  > /root/misp-bootstrap-api-key)
su -m www -c '/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin updateJSON'
su -m www -c '/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin schemaDiagnostics'
```

Keep the bootstrap API key private.
Wait for `All JSON structures updated` before continuing.
Confirm that diagnostics show `Pending: 0` and `Failed: 0`.

### Set up the instance signing key {#openbsd-install-gnupg}

Create the instance key in a private Bash session and substitute your instance's email address.

```bash
install -d -o www -g www -m 0700 /var/db/misp/gnupg
read -r -s -p 'Instance GnuPG passphrase: ' gpg_passphrase
printf '\n'
printf '%s\n' "$gpg_passphrase" | su -m www -c \
  'gpg --homedir /var/db/misp/gnupg --batch --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase-fd 0 \
  --quick-generate-key misp@example.org ed25519 sign never'
unset gpg_passphrase
su -m www -c 'gpg --homedir /var/db/misp/gnupg --armor --export \
  misp@example.org > /var/www/MISP/app/webroot/gpg.asc'
```

Set `GnuPG.binary` to `/usr/local/bin/gpg` in `app/Config/config.php`.
Set `GnuPG.homedir`, `GnuPG.email`, and `GnuPG.password` to the directory, address, and passphrase you used.
Include the key and configuration in your protected backups. [Instance and user keys](../cryptographic-keys/index.qmd)

## Serve MISP over HTTPS {#openbsd-install-web}

This setup uses the `apache2` service from the `apache-httpd` package.
In `/etc/apache2/httpd2.conf`, enable the `rewrite` and `ssl` modules, keep `headers` and the prefork MPM enabled, and add `Include /etc/apache2/extra/misp.conf`.
Keep the packaged include for `/var/www/conf/modules/*.conf`.

Create `/var/www/conf/modules/php-8.3.conf` with the PHP module and the handler for PHP scripts.

```apache
LoadModule php_module /usr/local/lib/apache2/php-8.3/libphp.so
<FilesMatch "\.php$">
    SetHandler application/x-httpd-php
</FilesMatch>
```

Create `/etc/apache2/extra/misp.conf`, substituting your DNS name and certificate paths.
Keep the packaged example SSL configuration disabled so Apache listens on port 443 once.

```apache
Listen 443

<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName misp.example.org
    Redirect permanent / https://misp.example.org/
</VirtualHost>

<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName misp.example.org
    DocumentRoot /var/www/MISP/app/webroot
    SSLEngine on
    SSLCertificateFile /etc/ssl/misp-fullchain.pem
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/ssl/private/misp.key

    <Directory /var/www/MISP/app/webroot>
        Options -Indexes +FollowSymLinks
        AllowOverride FileInfo
        Require all granted
        DirectoryIndex index.php
    </Directory>
</VirtualHost>
```

`AllowOverride FileInfo` enables the rewrite and API authorization rules in `app/webroot/.htaccess`.
Check the configuration and start Apache.

```bash
apachectl2 configtest
rcctl enable apache2
rcctl start apache2
```

Verify the certificate and HTTP redirect from a trusted client.
Sign in as `admin@admin.test` with password `admin` and change the password before opening the site to other clients. [First steps after login](../quick-start/index.qmd#first-steps-after-login)

## Start and verify the background workers {#openbsd-install-workers}

Use Supervisor's local Unix socket and give the `www` group access to it.
In `/etc/supervisord.conf`, edit the existing `[unix_http_server]` section and keep the packaged `[rpcinterface:supervisor]`, `[supervisorctl]`, and `[include]` sections.

```ini
[unix_http_server]
file=/var/run/supervisor/supervisor.sock
chmod=0660
chown=root:www
```

Create one worker for each queue and one dedicated scheduler.

```bash
install -d -m 0755 /etc/supervisord.d
{
  printf '%s\n' '[group:misp-workers]' 'programs=default,email,cache,prio,update,scheduler'
  for worker in default email cache prio update scheduler; do
    if [ "$worker" = scheduler ]; then
      cake_command=scheduler_worker
    else
      cake_command="start_worker $worker"
    fi
    cat <<CONFIG

[program:$worker]
command=/var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake $cake_command
directory=/var/www/MISP
user=www
environment=PATH="/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin",HOME="/var/db/misp"
autostart=true
autorestart=true
redirect_stderr=true
stdout_logfile=/var/www/MISP/app/tmp/logs/$worker-worker.log
CONFIG
  done
} > /etc/supervisord.d/misp-workers.ini
```

In the `SimpleBackgroundJobs` section of `app/Config/config.php`, set `redis_host` to `127.0.0.1` and `supervisor_host` to `unix:/var/run/supervisor/supervisor.sock`.
Set `supervisor_user` and `supervisor_password` to empty strings for the local socket.
Set `MISP.background_jobs` to `true`.

```bash
rcctl enable supervisord
rcctl start supervisord
rcctl order mysqld redis apache2 supervisord
rcctl check mysqld redis apache2 supervisord
supervisorctl status 'misp-workers:*'
netstat -na -f inet -p tcp
netstat -na -f inet6 -p tcp
```

Confirm that all six Supervisor processes are running and that MariaDB and Redis listen only on loopback.
MISP's `Admin getWorkers` uses a `ps` field that OpenBSD lacks, so the reported worker owner can be blank.
To check ownership, take the PID from `supervisorctl status` and run `ps -o user= -p PID`.
Save and search for an unpublished, organization-only test event and confirm that a queued job completes. [Background worker checks](../administration/index.qmd#admin-background-jobs)

## Plan a 2.5 upgrade {#openbsd-install-upgrade}

Use the shared [offline 2.5-to-3.0 upgrade](../upgrade-2-5-to-3-0/index.qmd) for backups, rehearsals, and database validation.
Follow the tracked `3.0_wip` branch, run the Cake commands as `www` with `su -m www -c`, and restart the packaged PHP module with `rcctl restart apache2` after the migration.
Time `Admin runUpgrade` on a restored copy before estimating your maintenance window.
